requirement: Demonstrate AI-managed amateur radio operations from LEO
Provide amateur radio operators with transponder access
Demonstrate graceful degradation to conventional operation
Advance TinyML/TinyLM technology for space applications
Engage amateur radio community in space communications
The mission shall have a design life of 12 months minimum
The spacecraft shall be capable of autonomous operations for up to 7 days without ground contact

The spacecraft shall re-enter the atmosphere no later than 5 years after completion of the mission with disposal success probability ≥ 0.9 (47 CFR 97.207(g)(1)(vii)(D)(1)), and within 25 years after mission completion per NASA-STD-8719.14C. *(Changed from the 25-year rule by the funding audit, 2026-10-14; see `docs/regulatory/filings/ODAR_SMART-QSO.md`.)*
The mission shall operate in Low Earth Orbit (LEO)
The nominal orbit altitude shall be 400-500 km
The orbit inclination shall support global amateur radio coverage

The deployment altitude shall not exceed 500 km unless NASA DAS shows MRD-003 is met with the solar wings undeployed, and shall not exceed 525 km in any case. *(Added by the funding audit, 2026-10-14; see `docs/BASELINE_PARAMETERS.md` §3.)*

The spacecraft shall transmit a beacon at least every 60 seconds in ACTIVE mode, and at least every 180 seconds in IDLE and SAFE to save power (`docs/BEACON_SPEC.md` §7), unless a transmit inhibit is active
The beacon shall include spacecraft health telemetry
The spacecraft shall be detectable by amateur ground stations
The downlink frequency shall be coordinated with IARU
The downlink shall comply with all applicable amateur radio regulations
All transmissions shall be in the clear (no encryption) per Part 97

The AI shall predict regional amateur radio demand
The AI shall prioritize QSOs fairly
The AI shall compose dynamic beacon messages
AI operations shall not compromise spacecraft safety
The spacecraft shall generate sufficient power for all mission modes
The spacecraft shall survive eclipse periods of up to 35 minutes
Power-intensive operations shall be duty-cycled based on power availability
AI payload power consumption shall be managed to maintain positive power budget
The spacecraft shall detumble within 7 days of deployment
The spacecraft shall maintain attitude knowledge sufficient for antenna pointing
The spacecraft shall stabilize attitude for nominal operations
The mission shall support ground station reception using amateur equipment
Beacon telemetry shall be decodable by amateur operators
The mission shall coordinate with amateur satellite tracking networks
The spacecraft shall comply with all launch provider safety requirements
The spacecraft shall not create debris during nominal operations
The spacecraft shall passivate at end of life
The spacecraft shall be trackable by ground-based surveillance
The mission shall obtain IARU frequency coordination

The spacecraft shall implement watchdog protection on all processors
The spacecraft shall be capable of autonomous recovery from single-event upsets

The EPS shall generate minimum 2W orbit-average power
The EPS shall incorporate body-mounted and/or deployable solar arrays

The transmitter shall support AFSK 1200 bps modulation
Spurious emissions shall be at least 40 dB below carrier

If no authenticated telecommand is received for N days, the spacecraft shall cease all transmissions, keep the telecommand receiver on, and resume only after an authenticated telecommand; N shall be configurable by telecommand within 1–90 days (default and range TBR per decision D3), and the elapsed time shall persist across resets *(added 2026-10-15; SQSO-ICD-013 §6.2; IARU 7.9)*

The spacecraft shall cease all RF emissions on an authenticated telecommand in every operating mode, and also on an unauthenticated TX-OFF telecommand whenever no telecommand key is usable; shall keep emissions ceased across resets until an authenticated telecommand re-enables them; and shall keep the telecommand receiver powered while ceased (47 CFR 97.207(b); ITU RR 22.1) *(added 2026-10-15; SQSO-ICD-013)*

requirement: Frequency accuracy shall be within 5 kHz *(renumbered 2026-10-16 from a second SYS-204; SYS-204 is TX-OFF)*
The spacecraft shall transmit AX.25 formatted beacons

Beacon interval shall be 60 s in ACTIVE, 120 s in IDLE and 180 s in SAFE, unless a transmit inhibit is active (`docs/BASELINE_PARAMETERS.md` §8) *[PI to ratify. Amended 2026-10-16 from "configurable from 10 to 120 seconds" to the baseline. The SET_BEACON telecommand still accepts only 10 to 120 s (SQSO-ICD-013 §7), so 180 s cannot be commanded]*
Beacons shall include spacecraft callsign
Beacons shall include health telemetry in machine-readable format
Beacons shall include human-readable information field
Beacon content shall be generated by AI when available, template fallback otherwise
The antenna shall deploy after separation from deployer

Antenna and solar-array deployment shall be inhibited until 30 minutes after deployment switch activation (CDS Rev 14.1 §2.4.4). A power-on, brownout or unknown reset or a stowed switch shall restart the wait (CDS §2.3.2.4); a watchdog or software reset shall not shorten it; deployment attempts shall persist across resets and be bounded, and an element sensed as deployed shall not be fired *(reset rules added 2026-10-15; `deployment.h`)*
The antenna shall provide omnidirectional coverage
Antenna VSWR shall be less than 2:1 at operating frequency

The spacecraft shall not generate or transmit any RF signal earlier than 45 minutes after on-orbit deployment (CDS Rev 14.1 §2.4.5), and the timer shall reset if a deployment switch toggles (CDS §2.3.2.4). A power-on, brownout or unknown reset shall restart the timer; a watchdog or software reset shall not shorten it; no telecommand shall shorten or clear it *(added by the funding audit, 2026-10-14; reset rules 2026-10-15; SQSO-ICD-013 §6.3)*

The spacecraft shall have at least three independent physical inhibits between the battery and each RF transmitter, and between the battery and each deployable actuator; RBF pins and timers do not count (CDS Rev 14.1 §2.3.7, §2.3.8) *(added by the funding audit, 2026-10-14)*
